bib.title: Do Embodied Agents Dream of Pixelated Sheep?: Embodied Decision Making using Language Guided World Modelling

question: Can few-shot LLM-hypothesized subgoal graphs, verified through environment experience, make RL exploration in Minecraft item crafting more sample efficient while tolerating LLM errors?
hypothesis: If LLMs are used to improve exploration during training rather than to generate plans at execution time, the resulting policies will not be constrained by LLM accuracy.
contributions: DECKARD: Dream/Wake loop that hypothesizes an Abstract World Model (AWM) DAG of subgoals with a few-shot LLM and verifies/corrects it with experience
Modular subgoal policies via adapters on VPT
Order-of-magnitude sample efficiency gain and robustness to injected AWM errors

method.summary: Codex is prompted once at the start of training to write a python dict of recipes for 391 Minecraft items, giving a hypothesized DAG (AWM). Dream phase samples a branch to a frontier node on the predicted path to the goal; Wake phase runs per-subgoal VPT+adapter PPO policies, verifies or corrects edges, and trains a new subgoal policy for each newly verified node.
method.task: Minecraft item crafting/collecting (RL exploration) and open-ended exploration

datasets.name: Minecraft via MineDojo 'creative' metatask
datasets.split: subgoal training on a single world seed where target is nearby; evaluation on random world seeds
datasets.preprocessing: AWM parsed from Codex python dict; plank/wood variants mapped to planks, cane to reeds; 4 circular dependencies removed

other.use: generates AWM once before training; no LLM forward passes during training or inference

models.name: VPT-a (VPT bc-house-3x + Houlsby adapters)
models.params: 0.5B VPT; 9.5M trainable adapter params per subgoal
models.architecture: transformer with two adapter modules per layer, 16x hidden reduction

training.objective: PPO with value head, KL loss to non-finetuned VPT replacing entropy, MineClip reward shaping plus +1 on target item
training.steps: limit 6 million environment steps per agent (stone pickaxe task: 2.6M DECKARD, 32M No LLM, Table 2)
training.seeds: robustness runs: at least three random seeds per error type and rate; otherwise not stated

inference.samples: one AWM generation over 391 items; Codex generated parsable entries for all but one (brown mushroom block)
inference.prompting: code-comment instruction plus two examples (diamond pickaxe, diamond) in a python dict

metrics.name: AWM accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of items with correct collectable/craftable label, workbench, recipe ingredients, exact recipe

metrics.name: Task success rate
metrics.definition: obtaining target item within step cap, random world seeds

metrics.name: Environment steps to craft stone pickaxe

eval.protocol: Random world seeds for evaluation; AWM error injection robustness over >=3 seeds; no significance test stated

limits: Requires an environment already grounded in language (textual state, here inventory).
Assumes a given state abstraction; automatic discovery left to future work.
Only deterministic AWM transitions; keeps first experienced edge between nodes.
Comparison to other Minecraft agents is loose: different action/observation spaces, pretraining and shortcuts; uses discrete crafting actions.
Robustness evidence is injected synthetic errors, shown in a figure without numbers in text; LLM not queried during training so cannot re-plan.
Subgoal training on a single world seed; c0 value not stated; no compute or wall-clock reported.

terms.definition: a DAG over textual state abstractions (inventory) whose nodes are subgoals and edges are dependencies
sample a branch to a node on the verified frontier on the predicted path to the goal
execute subgoal policies along the branch, explore, verify nodes

figures.caption: During the Dream phase, DECKARD uses the LLM-predicted DAG of subgoals, the hypothesized AWM, to sample a node on the path to the current task. Then, during the Wake phase, the agent executes subgoals and explores until reaching the sampled node.
LLM guidance improves environment timestep efficiency by an order of magnitude
Effect of errors in the initial AWM

code.snippet: F <- Frontier(G,V); if any(C(F)<=c0): x_bar <- SampleBranch(F | C(F)<=c0) else x_bar <- SampleBranch(F u V); Wake: execute subgoals, add edge and verify new node
